title: Testing new World Boss mechanics in my solo-dev browser MMORPG (Velundra)
author: GastonSaillen
selftext:
Heavily inspired by Diablo 4 and WoW, I’m trying to hit a sweet spot between fast-paced ARPG action and classic MMO raid mechanics. Here I'm testing a new World Boss encounter featuring a 3-phase escalation system—as its health drops, it ramps up aggression, chains abilities faster, and spawns waves of adds. (The extra characters running around are stress-test bots I spun up to test server tick rates, concurrency, and combat sync).

The entire game is built from scratch in pure TypeScript and Babylon.js without a traditional game engine. For the pipeline, I generate base 3D assets locally using diffusion models, clean and optimize them heavily in Blender with custom Python scripts, and hand-craft the world layout myself (AI is still terrible at natural level placement).

This is **Ferrums**, the second zone in the game, which took me about a month to build and is still getting iterated on. Right now, the game has over 30 hours of quests, free roam, world events, custom armor sets, and a player economy. Over 150 players have jumped in so far, and I'm currently working full-time on the 3rd out of 6 planned zones while squashing bugs daily.

Looking at the boss fight in the clip, what would you tweak or add to make the mechanics feel more impactful?
